name: a direct connection is one solid line
a two-way connection is a two-way line
an end rolls up to its nearest placed ancestor
a nearer placed ancestor wins over a farther one
an end under no placed element is not drawn
a connection inside one placed element is internal
several connections rolled up to one pair share a dashed line
parallel direct lines stay apart with detail
parallel direct lines merge without detail
a merged line with a direct member stays solid
a hidden transit element is bridged and its hop listed
a placed transit element that is on draws the real connections
a chain of hidden elements lists every hop in order
a chain of hidden elements longer than the hop limit joins nothing
a hidden dead end just disappears
bridging follows the direction of the connections
bridging against the direction draws nothing
two-way connections bridge once as a two-way line
a hidden element hides its subtree
a hidden connection is left out and does not bridge
a bridged line that lands inside one placed element is internal
a parent cycle ends the walk
a connection that realises an outer one is drawn to its boundary box
a boundary box whose element is placed is a marker with no line
one connection realising two outer connections is drawn to both boxes
a realising connection wholly inside draws between its own elements
a refinement to the element outside is drawn to its boundary box
a connection to an unplaced element under a hidden placed one is hidden with it
